task.description:
Combined WF-03 Step 0.5 (registry lookup) and Step 1 (diagnose), as ISS-0198's own run combined them. Read docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml in full first -- it is the task, and its `description` states explicitly what it does and does NOT pre-decide.

Do these, in order:

(1) REGISTRY LOOKUP (Step 0.5). Search docs/issues/*.yaml for prior entries about handoff size, verbosity, redundancy or pipeline latency. State whether this is a first occurrence or a recurrence of a root cause a prior fix failed to remove. Per WF-03 Step 0.5 rule 2, a genuine recurrence forces severity to at least MAJOR regardless of the record's current MINOR.

(2) VERIFY THE PREMISE BEFORE BUILDING ON IT. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 1.1 binds you here: ISS-0200's numbers were measured by ORCH on another run and are a checkable factual claim. ISS-0198's own diagnosis (handoffs/WF03-ISS0198-20260821/step-005-01-diagnose.json) overturned that issue's stated premise by measuring it, and the issue record was corrected rather than the measurement discarded. Do the same here: if your numbers disagree with ISS-0200's, your measurement wins and you say so.

(3) MEASURE FIRST-HAND, over at least three runs (AC1). Do NOT inherit ISS-0200's figures. handoffs/ holds ~585 JSON files across ~65 run directories; parse them with python and Jason-free json.load. At minimum derive, per handoff and pooled: len(result.summary); its ratio to len(task.description); the distribution (median/p90/p95/max) across the whole corpus; and how those compare to the dispatch-side figures in the Enforcement note's H-SIZE section of docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md. Quote real numbers and the code that produced them. Put any script in scratch/ per core-directives.md's File Placement Rules.

(4) ANSWER AC2 -- THE ACTUAL QUESTION. Is there a redundancy defect in result.summary that is DISTINCT from a summary being genuinely, justifiably long? This is the crux and it is not pre-decided. ISS-0200's record argues both sides itself: a dispatch restating a file it already names in artifacts_in is pure redundancy, whereas a result.summary is an ATTESTATION the acting agent owes first-hand. To answer it you need a mechanism, measured -- the dispatch-side answer was `cite-and-also-restate`, evidenced by all 20 corpus dispatches over 6,000 chars naming an artifacts_in basename inside the description. Find the equivalent mechanism for the result side, or establish by measurement that there is none. Candidate mechanisms worth testing rather than assuming: a summary restating content that already exists in a file named in its own artifacts_out; a summary restating its own issues[] entries in prose; a validator's summary restating the producer's summary; evidence (command output, counts, tables) inlined in prose where artifacts_out could carry it. Test the ones the corpus supports; report which you tested and which the data did not support.

(5) A REASONED NO-CHANGE VERDICT IS A LEGITIMATE OUTCOME and AC2 says so in terms. Do not manufacture a rule to look productive. If the measurement shows result.summary length is bought by genuine attestation, say that, with the evidence, and recommend NO-CHANGE.

(6) IF you conclude a fix is warranted, state WHAT it must change without writing it -- you are diagnosis, not implementation (WF-03 Step 1 rule 4). Say specifically: what the structured outlet should be (artifacts_out pointing at a written report, a required shape, or nothing), and why it does not weaken section 4's validator-re-derivation requirement or section 2's worked examples (AC4, and ISS-0200's closing DO-NOT). Say also whether a mechanical check should exist; if yes, note that AC5 requires it be added to ISS-0191's scope worded so nothing implies it runs today.

(7) CONFIRM OR REJECT THIS RUN'S SHAPE. ORCH's working assumption, from the WF03-ISS0198-20260821 precedent, is that Step 2 (CODE-DESIGNER) and Step 4 (regression test) are recorded SKIPPED with stated reasons -- the deliverable is prose in a protocol doc, so there are no module interfaces to design and no code under test. Confirm that, or reject it and say what should run instead. ORCH is deliberately not pre-deciding it.

Do NOT implement any fix, do not edit HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md, and do not edit docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml. Commit only your completed handoff file and any scratch script, per core-directives.md's File Placement Rules (scratch/ is git-ignored -- so in practice, only the handoff).
acceptance_criteria: Step 0.5 answered: prior-match search over docs/issues/*.yaml reported, with a first-occurrence-or-recurrence verdict and severity consequence stated
ISS-0200's own measured figures independently re-derived or contradicted, with the disagreement stated plainly if there is one (HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 1.1)
A first-hand measurement of len(result.summary) spanning at least three runs, with the producing code quoted and real distribution figures given -- not inherited from ISS-0200
An explicit verdict on whether result.summary carries a redundancy defect DISTINCT from justified length, naming the candidate mechanisms tested and which the corpus did or did not support

If a fix is recommended: what it must change, stated without writing it, plus why it does not weaken HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 4's validator-re-derivation requirement or section 2's worked examples. If NO-CHANGE: the evidence for that, stated as a verdict and not as an absence of findings
An explicit confirm-or-reject of ORCH's assumption that Step 2 and Step 4 are SKIPPED on this run
No fix implemented; HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md and docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml are unmodified (quote git status --porcelain to show it)

result.summary:
WF-03 Steps 0.5 + 1 combined -- ISS-0200. VERDICT: NO-CHANGE. result.summary carries no redundancy defect distinct from justified length. Stated as a verdict from measurement, not as an absence of findings.

=== STEP 0.5 -- REGISTRY LOOKUP ===
Searched all 127 docs/issues/*.yaml for handoff size / verbosity / redundancy / pipeline latency. Four matches, all read in full: ISS-0198 (resolved, the dispatch half, 2026-08-21), ISS-0191 (open, the linter that would host any mechanical check), ISS-0201 (open, three wording riders on the same section), ISS-0117 (the run whose cost surfaced the family). FIRST OCCURRENCE, NOT A RECURRENCE. ISS-0198's fix targeted task.description and, on its own terms, removed a root cause there; ISS-0200 is the deliberately-deferred SECOND HALF of the same investigation, not the same defect resurfacing after a failed fix. WF-03 Step 0.5 rule 2 therefore does not fire and severity stays MINOR. (For completeness: ISS-0198's fix also demonstrably held on this run -- see SELF-MEASUREMENT below.)

=== STEP 1 (2) -- ISS-0200'S PREMISE, INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED (HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 1.1) ===
Every figure in ISS-0200's description was re-derived first-hand from handoffs/*.json with json.load. ALL CONFIRMED EXACTLY, no disagreement to report:
  - WF03-ISS0117-20260821: sum(len(result.summary)) = 143,465 vs sum(len(task.description)) = 68,348 -> 2.099x. Matches "143,465 / 68,348 / 2.1x".
  - Largest file on that run: step-03d-reviewer-regate.json at 41,723 bytes, desc 6,290, summary 24,369. Matches all three.
  - WF03-ISS0198-20260821 dispatches: 1,999 / 3,074 / 2,451 chars; their summaries 20,095 / 9,021 / 12,104. Matches all six.
ONE FIGURE TO CORRECT AS A GENERALISATION, not as an error: "2.1x" is that ONE RUN's ratio, and ISS-0200's title generalises it ("the larger half of the artefact"). Pooled corpus-wide the gap is WIDER, not narrower -- 2,599,136 summary chars vs 889,118 description chars = 2.92x over 605 files. The premise is not merely true, it understates. Corpus is 605 parseable / 0 unparseable across 60 run directories (ISS-0198 measured 582, its REVIEWER 586; growth is this-day runs, and the parse rate is still 100%).

=== STEP 1 (3) -- FIRST-HAND DISTRIBUTION, 605 FILES / 60 RUNS (well over AC1's three) ===
Producing code: scratch/iss0200_measure.py (scratch/ is git-ignored per core-directives.md File Placement Rules, so it is not committed; its core is reproduced here verbatim).

    for f in sorted(glob.glob('handoffs/**/*.json', recursive=True)):
        if os.path.basename(f) == 'registry.json': continue
        d = json.load(open(f, encoding='utf-8'))
        t = d.get('task') or {}; r = d.get('result') or {}; c = d.get('context') or {}
        recs.append(dict(desc=t.get('description') or '', summ=r.get('summary') or '',
                         ain=c.get('artifacts_in') or [], aout=r.get('artifacts_out') or [],
                         issues=r.get('issues') or [], size=os.path.getsize(f)))

  len(result.summary), n=605:   median 2,986  p90 8,493  p95 12,323  max 47,036  mean 4,296  total 2,599,136
  len(task.description), n=605: median 704    p90 3,940  p95 5,737   max 19,040  mean 1,470  total 889,118
  per-handoff ratio summ/desc (n=601 with both): median 3.53x  p90 13.86x  p95 19.37x  max 43.5x
COMPARISON TO THE H-SIZE FIGURES IN THE ENFORCEMENT NOTE (measured there over 582 files: desc median 682, p90 3,191, p95 5,138, max 12,187). My desc figures track them closely -- the drift (p90 3,191 -> 3,940, max 12,187 -> 19,040) is the ISS-0119 run's step-02-code-designer at 19,040, which post-dates that measurement. THE RESULT SIDE SITS AN ORDER OF MAGNITUDE HIGHER AT EVERY QUANTILE: summary median 2,986 exceeds the description p90; summary p95 (12,323) roughly equals the description MAX that H-SIZE-1's 6,000 threshold was set to select the tail of. 120 of 605 summaries (19.8%) exceed 6,000 chars, against 26 of 605 descriptions (4.3%). So "6,000 selects a 3.4% tail" is a dispatch-side property that does NOT transfer: the same number on the result side selects a fifth of the corpus, i.e. the norm.

=== STEP 1 (4) -- AC2: IS THERE A REDUNDANCY DEFECT DISTINCT FROM JUSTIFIED LENGTH? ===
The dispatch-side answer was a MECHANISM, measured: cite-and-also-restate, evidenced by 20/20 over-6,000 dispatches naming an artifacts_in basename inside the description, plus an empty structured outlet (requirement_text == {} in 66 of 69) while copied source rode in prose. I looked for the result-side equivalent. Population under test: the 120 summaries over 6,000 chars. Method: 8-word-shingle set overlap, reported as the fraction of the SUMMARY's shingles also present in the comparison text -- so a summary that is mostly restatement scores high regardless of the source's size.

FIVE-PLUS CANDIDATE MECHANISMS TESTED. NONE SUPPORTED. Not one of the 120 exceeded 0.30 overlap on ANY axis:
  M1 summary restates a file named in its own artifacts_out   -- n=35 usable pairs, median 0.059, max 0.264, >0.30: 0/35. (Structural screen, the direct H-SIZE-1 analogue: only 46/120 big summaries even NAME an artifacts_out basename, vs 20/20 on the dispatch side. The screen does not select.)
  M2 summary restates its own issues[] entries in prose       -- n=130, median 0.009, p90 0.075, max 0.162.
  M3 validator summary restates the producer's summary        -- n=248 validator/producer pairs, median 0.002, p90 0.029, max 0.200. This one matters most: it is direct positive evidence that section 4's re-derivation requirement is being honoured rather than echoed.
  M5 summary echoes back its own task.description             -- n=120, median 0.002, max 0.069.
  M6 summary restates ANY earlier summary in the same run     -- n=100, median 0.007, max 0.162.
  M7 (added) summary restates a file it names in artifacts_in -- n=119, median 0.018, max 0.264.

METHOD HONESTY -- THE CALIBRATION IS THE WEAK POINT AND I AM REPORTING IT, NOT HIDING IT. Run against the 26 big DISPATCHES, the same 8-gram method gives median 0.054, p90 0.200, max 0.347 versus artifacts_in content -- i.e. it barely separates the dispatch side either, because ISS-0198's cite-and-restate was PARAPHRASE, not verbatim copy, and verbatim shingles are under-powered against paraphrase. So M1-M7 alone would be weak evidence. They are load-bearing only in the COMPARATIVE form: on every axis the result side scores at or BELOW the dispatch side (result max 0.264 < dispatch max 0.347; result p90 0.167 < dispatch p90 0.200). The result side is not worse than the side already ruled acceptable in its non-restated part.

TWO INDEPENDENT LINES CARRY THE VERDICT, because the shingle test cannot:
  (a) EVIDENCE DENSITY. Split each summary into >25-char segments; count segments carrying a digit, a file path, or an identifier (REQ-\d, INV-\d, foo/2). Big summaries: median 65.3% evidence-bearing, p10 54.7%, MIN 36.7%. Big descriptions: median 60.1%, p10 41.0%, min 30.9%. Digit fraction in big summaries: median 0.0295, p90 0.0490 -- 3-5x ordinary English prose. Long summaries are long because they carry MORE first-hand measurement per sentence, not less. Restatement would dilute this ratio; it is instead the highest in the corpus.
  (b) I READ THE HARDEST CASE BY HAND -- the least-evidence-dense LARGE summary, handoffs/WF02-REQ027-20260816/step-02c-security-reviewer.json (34,681 chars, density 0.440, the worst-scoring big one and the 2nd largest in the corpus). Its content is: a re-derived scope test explicitly refusing ORCH's ("re-derived, not inherited from ORCH"), an INV-1..INV-8 determination table with all 8 verdicts, __info__(:functions) output probed live, quoted cleanup output, and a "WHAT I DID NOT FIND" section. It restates its artifacts_in nowhere. If the thesis fails anywhere it fails here, and it holds here.

WHY THE TWO SIDES ARE GENUINELY ASYMMETRIC, which is the answer to the question ISS-0200 refused to pre-decide: the dispatch-side defect had TWO halves -- a duplicated copy AND an empty structured outlet it should have travelled in. Neither half exists here. There is no result-side field sitting empty while its content rides in prose: artifacts_out is non-empty on 449 of 605 handoffs, and where it points at a real produced artefact the summary does NOT duplicate it (M1, max 0.264). A duplicated copy is unmeasurable and drifts from its source -- that was ISS-0198's whole case. An attestation has no source to drift from; it IS the source, and section 4 makes the acting agent the only party that can write it. Length bought by attestation is not the same object as length bought by duplication, and the corpus says this is the former.

=== STEP 1 (5)(6) -- WHAT A FIX MUST CHANGE: NOTHING IN HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md ===
NO-CHANGE. Do not extend section 2's inline-vs-artifacts_in table to result.summary, do not add a result-side length target, do not add a required shape. Positive reasons, not absence of findings:
  1. The mechanism such a rule would target does not exist in the corpus (M1/M2/M3/M5/M6/M7 above, 0/120 over 0.30 on every axis).
  2. Any such rule would collide head-on with section 4's re-derivation requirement and section 2's worked examples -- which ISS-0200's own closing DO-NOT forbids weakening. M3's median of 0.002 shows validators already write independent prose; the only way to shorten a validator summary materially is to state fewer re-derived checks, which is exactly the thing section 4 requires and the security-reviewer-scoped worked example ("an unlisted invariant reads as an unrun check") makes explicit.
  3. H-SIZE-2's logic applies with more force here than on the dispatch side. ISS-0198 established under-specification as the dominant latency term. A truncated result.summary does not just under-specify one step; it under-specifies every downstream step that reads it, and section 6 ("never satisfy a gate by editing what it measures") would be bought off by deletion.
MECHANICAL CHECK -- YES, BUT REPORTING ONLY, AND NO WARN. Recommend ISS-0191's scope gain ONE extension to the EXISTING H-SIZE-3 INFO reporter: emit median/max/total len(result.summary) alongside the len(desc) figures it already emits, plus the summ/desc ratio. No threshold, no WARN, no pass/fail -- a WARN would be a length rule by the back door and would be correctly discarded by the next agent who checked. Its sole purpose is that if the result side ever DOES acquire a restatement mechanism, the drift is visible without a fresh investigation. Per AC5 the wording added to ISS-0191 must sit under the Enforcement note's existing "Specified but NOT YET RUNNING" heading and must state plainly that it does not run today; ISS-0191 is open, unbuilt and gated on ISS-0190, and nothing about this extension changes that.

=== STEP 1 (7) -- RUN SHAPE: ORCH'S ASSUMPTION CONFIRMED, WITH ONE ADDITION ORCH MUST ACT ON ===
CONFIRMED for Step 2 (CODE-DESIGNER) and Step 4 (regression test): SKIPPED, precedent WF03-ISS0198-20260821 and WF03-ISS0117-20260821. No module interfaces to design; a regression test would have to assert over handoffs/*.json, which zero ExUnit tests do (grep -rn "handoffs/" test/ --include=*.exs returns only provenance comments), and shipping a partial linter as this run's regression test is what ISS-0191 exists to prevent.
ADDITION ORCH DID NOT PRE-DECIDE AND MUST NOW DECIDE: a NO-CHANGE verdict also empties STEP 3. There is no amendment to implement, so no ELIXIR-DEV/DOC-UPDATER edit to HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md, and therefore nothing for SECURITY-REVIEWER to gate. I recommend Step 3 be recorded SKIPPED-as-implementation but that a REVIEWER gate still run ON THIS DIAGNOSIS, not on a diff -- core-directives.md's "every producing step has a validating step" is not suspended by the producing step concluding "no change", and a NO-CHANGE verdict that no second role checked is exactly the shape of an unvalidated claim. The run then goes Step 1 -> REVIEWER gate -> Step 5 (close) -> Step Final. The only files this run should change are docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml at Step 5 and the ISS-0191 scope sentence above.
STATUS-VOCABULARY GAP FLAGGED FOR STEP 5: ISSUE_QUEUE.md's vocabulary has no terminal status for "investigated, measured, no defect found." resolved asserts "a root cause was actually removed, and a regression test proves it" -- false here, nothing was removed. instrumented asserts real work shipped with the root cause still present -- also false, nothing shipped. Filed as a MINOR issue below; ORCH should rule at Step 5 rather than let ISSUE-FIXER pick one silently.

=== SELF-MEASUREMENT (this run, since the issue family is about handoff size) ===
This run's two dispatches: 640 and 4,461 chars of task.description. Neither trips H-SIZE-1 (both under 6,000) nor H-SIZE-2. The 4,461-char one names artifacts_in basenames but does not restate them -- it cites ISS-0200 and ISS-0198's diagnosis by path and tells me to read them, which is precisely the shape section 2 prescribes. ISS-0198's fix is holding. This summary is itself over 6,000 chars, which is the norm for a diagnosis step (ISSUE-FIXER diagnoses in the corpus measure 29,661 / 25,455 / 24,079 / 20,095 / 19,714) and is, by its own argument, bought by attestation.

=== AC7 -- NO FIX IMPLEMENTED ===
git status --porcelain at completion:
     M handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-005-01-diagnose.json
Exactly one file, this handoff. docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md and docs/issues/ISS-0200.yaml are unmodified and do not appear. Measurement scripts live in scratch/ (git-ignored, .gitignore line 38 "/scratch/") per core-directives.md's File Placement Rules, so nothing else is committable.

issues.description: ISSUE_QUEUE.md's issue-status vocabulary has no terminal state for an issue that was investigated and measured to have no defect. `resolved` asserts a root cause was removed and a regression test proves it; `instrumented` asserts verified work shipped with the root cause intact. Neither is true of a NO-CHANGE outcome, which WF-03 and ISS-0200's own AC5 explicitly license. ORCH should rule for this run's Step 5 and consider filing the vocabulary gap as its own issue.

Adjacent finding, surfaced while measuring artifacts_out and not part of ISS-0200's question: 190 of the 449 handoffs with a non-empty result.artifacts_out list THEIR OWN handoff file as one of their outputs (85 of the 120 over-6,000-char summaries do). Section 2 defines artifacts_out as the artefacts the step produced; a handoff file is not an output of its own result block, and the self-reference makes the field useless as a machine-readable index of what a run produced. Candidate for ISS-0190's data-defect scope or a check in ISS-0191's linter. Filed as an observation only -- I did not diagnose it.

Method limitation, recorded so a later reader does not over-read this diagnosis: the 8-word-shingle overlap test used for mechanisms M1-M7 detects VERBATIM restatement and is under-powered against paraphrase -- calibrated against the 26 over-6,000-char dispatches (the population ISS-0198 established as true positives by reading them), it returns median 0.054 / max 0.347, so it does not cleanly separate that side either. The NO-CHANGE verdict therefore rests on the comparative form of those figures plus two independent lines (evidence-density and a hand-read of the worst-scoring large summary), not on the shingle numbers alone.

result.next_action: NO-CHANGE verdict -- there is no fix to design. Do NOT route to CODE-DESIGNER (WF-03 Step 2 SKIPPED, no module interfaces for a prose verdict); Step 4 SKIPPED (no ExUnit test asserts over handoffs/*.json; deferred to ISS-0191). Recommend ORCH route this diagnosis to REVIEWER as a gate on the NO-CHANGE verdict itself, then Step 5 (close ISS-0200 with the NO-CHANGE resolution and add the H-SIZE-3 result.summary reporting line to ISS-0191's scope), then Step Final.
